name: memory-loop-scenario
description: Declarative walk-through data for the living-memory loop, about the `memory-loop-demo` capability defined in 01-baseline.json: a session that produced observations, four staged claims spanning the three states the curation queue handles (linked, unlinked, and a contested pair), one proposal already open for review, one capability request raised against the demo capability's owner, and one auto-promote allowlist entry. This mirrors, as data, the exact sequence tests/integration/test_memory_loop_e2e.py exercises against a live database by calling ClaimService, ConsolidationService, and PromotionService directly -- a human walking the curation-queue and promotion-review surfaces by hand can reproduce it claim by claim from this file.
loader_status: scripts/seed.py does not execute the sections below yet, and this is deliberate rather than an oversight: `session_events`, `staged_claims`, `promotion_proposals`, `capability_requests`, and `autopromote_allowlist` are not in the loader's allowed top-level section set, because every one of the tables they describe is owned by exactly one service (memory_claims, for instance, may only be written by ClaimService -- a structural rule a lint gate enforces) rather than by the generic entity/attribute upsert the loader performs for catalog data. Writing these rows correctly means calling those services, not re-deriving their invariants (confidence scoring, authority derivation, visibility inheritance, the confidence/promotion CHECK constraints) a second time in a seed script. `make seeds-validate` passes on this file today -- it is schema-only and only ever inspects `entities`/`bitemporal_attributes`, neither of which this file declares. `make dev-seed` will raise 'unknown top-level key(s)' if it walks this file, until a loader extension exists that calls ClaimService/ConsolidationService/PromotionService/the capability-request and guardrail services the way the integration test does. That extension is follow-up work, not part of this bundle. Separately, and also required before this scenario could be produced by `make dev-seed`: the memory ontology's predicates (`owned_by_team`, `lifecycle_state`, `runbook_url`, referenced below) are seeded today only by `claim_ontology.seed_ontology`, which nothing outside the test suite calls yet -- a fresh dev database has no memory predicates until something invokes it.

session_events.body: Who owns the memory-loop-demo capability, what's its lifecycle state, and who owns the upcoming mobile checkout redesign?

Observed from the conversation: the platform team owns memory-loop-demo, it is GA, and the mobile checkout redesign (no matching capability in this tenant) is owned by the checkout team. Staged as claims for review.
